payload.body:
You are willing to change the plan when you realize it no longer fits. New information, a better way of doing something, or simply wanting something different can be enough for you to reconsider a choice other people assumed was already decided.

What feels like an obvious change to you can catch other people off guard because they usually hear about it after you have already spent time questioning what was no longer working.

The challenge is knowing when change is helping you build a life that fits better and when change itself has become the answer you reach for whenever something starts feeling too defined. Being known, expected, or counted on can feel restrictive even when nobody is actually preventing you from choosing differently.

The useful question is what changed. If your needs, priorities, information, or circumstances changed, the direction may need to change too. If the only problem is that someone now expects consistency from you, their expectation may still be having too much influence over the decision.
